trustModel.note: Bitcoin L1 is the canonical trust/finality root. External chains, networks, layers, assets, and staking adapters remain valid when independently evidenced.

sdkChainIdentifiers.meaning: SDK-local chain/network/layer identifiers; not a live-adapter or production-support count

builtinAssetRecords.meaning: Unique built-in chain-and-symbol records; inactive records are inventory-only and fail closed

protocolModules.meaning: Non-test protocol modules, including infrastructure and integration modules

capabilityEvidenceRecords.meaning: Evidence ledger rows across protocol, WASM, operations, release, identity, and attestation research; not 70 chains

exactCoreChainProjections.meaning: SDK identifiers that map exactly to the mirrored Core concrete-chain taxonomy without family collapse

claimRules: Never publish capability-evidence row totals as chain, network, layer, asset, or connector totals.
Known, implemented, integrated, independently reviewed, and production-supported are separate states.
A registered asset or chain identifier does not prove a live observer, router, signer, verifier, RPC connection, or production SLA.
Downstream consumers must negotiate exact capability identifiers and evidence status instead of relying on aggregate counts.
